subject: Archaeology
title: The Standard of Ur: War and Peace
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Standard of Ur: War and Peace.

hook.text: A wooden box covered in lapis lazuli and shell mosaics was found crushed in a tomb at Ur — it tells a story on each side.

buildup.text: One side shows war: chariots trampling enemies, soldiers marching prisoners.

discovery.text: The Standard of Ur is from about 2600 BCE. It is one of the earliest known examples of narrative art — a story told in pictures.

twist.text: No one knows what the object actually was. It was too small for a battle standard.

climax.text: The war-and-peace theme appears throughout human art. This 4,600-year-old box captured a duality that has never changed.

punchline.text: War on one side, peace on the other. Sumer understood the human condition 4,600 years ago.

quiz.question: What mystery surrounds the Standard of Ur?
options: The language on it has never been translated
No one knows what the object actually was — it may be a musical instrument's soundbox
It was found in a location hundreds of miles from Ur
